target.title: fix(android): bound structured chat image decoding
target.body:
Closes #105053

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users opening chat history containing a large structured image could make the app decode an unbounded base64 string before bitmap sampling, bypassing the limit already used for outbound and Markdown images.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the existing 300 KiB encoded-image budget to the chat model boundary, applies it while parsing structured image parts, and repeats the guard as the decoder's first instruction. Outbound attachments and Markdown data images continue using the same canonical limit; audio content is unchanged.

## User Impact

Oversized structured history images are skipped before base64 and bitmap allocation, reducing avoidable memory pressure and UI jank. Normal images, managed media references, Markdown images, outgoing attachments, and audio retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Parser regression: a 307,201-character structured image is retained as metadata but its inline payload is dropped before rendering.
- Decoder regression: the same oversized input returns before Android `Base64.decode`, bitmap bounds, hashing, or caching.
- Existing Markdown boundary test now consumes the shared canonical constant.
- Structured Codex autoreview cycle 1 caught missing test imports after the constant move; both were fixed. Final autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox proof is unavailable: two fresh leases were terminated by the provider during hydration. The PR must not land until canonical hosted Android Play/third-party tests, build/lint, and ktlint pass on the exact SHA.

Provenance: structured content parsing was introduced in `d86ed21f3d6c3` by Ayaan Zaidi. Image previews in #104620 made the missing structured-image boundary user-visible; this fix preserves contributor credit without attributing the fix itself to either prior author.

target.title: fix: keep MCP Apps aligned with runtime tool policy
target.body:
Related: #69039

AI-assisted: implementation and review were performed with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where MCP App previews could disappear when optional resource listing failed, App-only tools could escape the originating run's effective tool policy, repeated preview-read failures could pause normal MCP calls, applied sandbox CSP was not advertised to the App, and Apps listener changes appeared hot-reloadable even though they require a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows up on the review feedback from #69039. It evaluates the complete MCP tool catalog, including App-only tools, through the same runtime and layered policy pipeline as model-visible tools; keeps optional preview discovery outside server-failure backoff; advertises the CSP actually applied by the host; and classifies `mcp.apps` listener changes as restart-required. Sandbox parent authentication is intentionally outside this follow-up.

## User Impact

MCP Apps remain available when servers omit or fail optional listing, App calls cannot exceed the tool policy of the run that opened the view, preview failures no longer disable unrelated MCP calls, Apps receive accurate CSP capabilities, and listener configuration changes take effect predictably after restart.

## Evidence

- Focused hosted tests: 538 assertions passed across MCP runtime, materialization, policy, Gateway, reload, and Control UI coverage.

target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses array-index path formatting for Zod-derived validation issues; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatConfigPath()` previously joined every segment with `.`, regardless of whether the segment was a string key or a numeric array index. This change formats numeric path segments with brackets while leaving string segments in dot notation.

The change stays inside config validation diagnostics and does not alter config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, or runtime config behavior.

## User Impact

Users reading config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties in schema-derived paths:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

The same formatting now applies to nested validation paths such as `bindings[0].url` and model-list validation paths such as `models.providers.openai-codex.models[0].api`.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both simple and nested numeric array-index paths:

```ts
["agents", "list", 0, "name"] -> "agents.list[0].name"
["agents", "list", 3, "tools", "profile"] -> "agents.list[3].tools.profile"
```

Validation run locally:

```powershell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
git diff --check -- src/config/validation.ts src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/config/validation.ts src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts
```

Results:

- focused Vitest run: `2 passed`, `50 tests passed`
- `git diff --check`: passed
- `oxfmt --check`: all 3 matched files use the correct format
Real behavior proof on current PR head (`f63b4b871d22df4768dcd3daea216be895bde7b7`):

```powershell
$env:OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH = "<temp>\\openclaw.json"
$env:OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR = "<temp>"
$env:NO_COLOR = "1"
node scripts/run-node.mjs config validate
node scripts/run-node.mjs config validate --json
```

Redacted invalid config payload:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      {
        "name": "proof-agent",
        "tools": {
          "exec": {
            "commandHighlighting": "not-a-boolean"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Normal output:

```text
OpenClaw config is invalid: <temp>\\openclaw.json
  × agents.list[0].id: Invalid input: expected string, received undefined
  × agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair, or fix the keys above manually.
Inspect with openclaw config validate.
```

JSON output:

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "path": "<temp>\\openclaw.json",
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "agents.list[0].id",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined"
    },
    {
      "path": "agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)",
      "allowedValues": [
        "true",
        "false"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config validation failure
  -> Zod issue path array
  -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()
  -> formatConfigPath()
  -> CLI/UI diagnostic path string
```

Affected surface is limited to config validation issue path display for numeric path segments coming through the shared Zod issue mapper. This PR intentionally leaves manual config validation paths, source line-number lookup, and bad-value redaction/rendering unchanged.

Closes #105068

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the Control UI shows the chat start screen — hero, recent chats, and the composer pinned at the bottom. Clicking "New session" in the sidebar opens `/new`, which is a differently shaped page: the composer sits mid-page between the target chips and the recent-chats list, anchored to the top of a scrolling page. The two "start working" surfaces looked unrelated and the composer jumped position between them.

## Why This Change Was Made

There should be one start-screen layout. The `/new` draft page now lays out exactly like the chat pane: the welcome hero and recent chats scroll in the middle, and the composer docks at the bottom with the target controls (agent, node, folder, worktree, base branch) directly above it.

- `new-session-page.ts` now renders a `__scroll` region (welcome) plus a bottom dock that reuses `.agent-chat__composer-shell` for geometry, so the draft composer aligns 1:1 with the chat composer.
- The page reuses `renderWelcomeState` from `chat-welcome.ts` (with a `hint` override) instead of maintaining its own hero/recents copies; the now single-consumer helpers (`renderWelcomeHero`, `renderWelcomeRecentSessions`, `renderWelcomeSuggestions`, `selectWelcomeRecentSessions`) are un-exported.
- The app shell treats `new-session` as a chat-like route (`content--chat`/`shell--chat`), so the pane owns its scrolling; the scroll container's top inset doubles as the native macOS titlebar drag band via `beginNativeWindowDragFromTopInset`, mirroring the chat thread.
- Draft-session semantics are unchanged: same target controls, same `sessions.create` payload, same redirect into the created chat.

## User Impact

The start screen and New Session are now visually one screen: composer always at the bottom, recent chats above it, and the "where does this session run" controls appear right above the composer on `/new`. Works across desktop and mobile widths.

Desktop:

![desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/new-session-unified-start/new-session-unified-desktop.png)

Free-text extraction had the same loose shape and could return Meet-like text that the runtime would later reject.

Calendar lookup should return only meeting URLs that already satisfy the same local contract used by runtime joins. This keeps `--today` / `--event` calendar selection from surfacing malformed or unsupported links that fail later in a different code path.

The extraction path now normalizes through one calendar-local helper that requires:

- `https:`
- `meet.google.com`
- a standard `xxx-xxxx-xxx` meeting-code path

Text extraction also avoids truncating longer tokens into fabricated meeting codes and trims sentence punctuation after query strings before URL normalization.

## User Impact

Users who select Google Meet sessions from Calendar get the same URL behavior as direct runtime joins. Invalid Calendar links are skipped instead of being selected and failing later when the meeting is joined.

target.title: fix(tavily): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the Tavily web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — Tavily is one of the web search providers that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. The web search runtime threads `signal` into `execute(args, { signal })`, but the Tavily provider ignored it — so aborted runs left Tavily requests open until their configured timeout.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted Tavily request caught by `runWebSearch`'s catch block can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Tavily signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the Tavily provider and client to `postTrustedWebToolsJson` (which already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141). The pattern matches the searxng fix in #104216 and the DuckDuckGo fix in #104899 — one provider per PR, no new SDK surface.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path Tavily uses:
- Production: `postTrustedWebToolsJson({ signal })` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`
- Proof: `withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint` — same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()` code path; only the SSRF policy differs (selfHosted allows localhost for proof).

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 122ms through guarded-fetch stack
        (withSelfHostedWebToolsEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:44061/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

Proof script: `extensions/tavily/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

### Signal chain — full path (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| Tavily provider tool | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts` | 28 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| Tavily POST helper | `extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts` | 90 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted POST endpoint | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 150 | `signal: params.signal` — native support |

No new SDK surface is needed — `postTrustedWebToolsJson` already accepts `signal?: AbortSignal` at line 141.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tavily/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ tavily tools: 15/15 passed (including signal forwarding test)
 ✓ tavily client: 5/5 passed
 ✓ runtime: 31/31 passed (including "does not fall back after parent cancellation")
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-client.ts \
    extensions/tavily/src/tavily-tools.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### Landing order

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) and #104899 (DuckDuckGo, same author) also add the same guard. Whichever lands first, the others will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: fix(config): apply Mistral maxTokens safe cap for all values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #105036.

`resolveNormalizedProviderModelMaxTokens()` only applied the per-model Mistral safe cap when the requested `maxTokens` value reached the model's full context window. Any explicit value between the safe cap and the context window was returned unchanged, allowing an invalid value to be used at runtime and in `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early-return condition `clamped < params.contextWindow` short-circuited the safe-cap lookup for all intermediate values. The fix removes that condition so the safe cap is evaluated for Mistral models, but **only** when the model id has an explicit entry in `MISTRAL_SAFE_MAX_TOKENS_BY_MODEL`. Unknown/custom Mistral ids keep the existing context-clamped value to avoid silently lowering existing configs.

## User Impact

Configuring a known Mistral model (e.g. `mistral-large-latest`) with `maxTokens` above the documented safe maximum now reliably clamps to that safe maximum, preventing provider-side rejections. Custom/unknown Mistral model settings are preserved.

## Evidence

### Unit tests
- Added focused helper tests in `src/config/defaults.test.ts`.
- Added config-loading regression tests through `applyModelDefaults`.
- Added doctor regression tests through `normalizeCompatibilityConfigValues`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/defaults.test.ts src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts` passes (79/79).
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json ...` reports 0 warnings/errors.

### Real after-fix behavior proof

Ran the real config-loading and doctor migration paths against a config containing a known model (`mistral-large-latest`, `maxTokens: 17000`) and a custom model (`custom-mistral-model`, `maxTokens: 32000`):

```text
=== After-fix behavior proof ===

1. Config loading path (applyModelDefaults):
  mistral-large-latest: maxTokens = 16384
  custom-mistral-model: maxTokens = 32000

2. Doctor migration path (normalizeCompatibilityConfigValues):
  mistral-large-latest: maxTokens = 16384
  custom-mistral-model: maxTokens = 32000

  Changes:
    - Normalized models.providers.mistral.models[0].maxTokens (17000 → 16384) to avoid Mistral context-window rejects.
```

The known model is clamped to its safe cap (`16384`), while the custom model remains unchanged.

target.title: fix(codex): prevent missing_tool_result from masking real abort/interrupt/failure outcomes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #104898.

When a Codex turn ends mid-exec (user abort, steer/interrupt, or stream failure) while a native `commandExecution` is still running, the synthesized `missing_tool_result` invariant was promoted to the run-level `promptError`. Operators saw a generic tool-invariant failure instead of abort/interrupt classification, and any partial assistant text was treated as a failed run.

## Root Cause

Two gaps combined to mask real outcomes:

1. `synthesizeMissingToolResults()` unconditionally promoted missing-tool errors to `promptError` for any non-completed turn, even when the authoritative outcome was already abort or interrupted.
2. In `buildResult()`, `synthesizedMissingToolResultError` took priority over `completedTurn.error.message`, so even for genuinely failed turns the real error could be masked.

## Fix — Two-layer defense

**Layer 1 (input guard):** In `synthesizeMissingToolResults()`, skip `recordPromptError` when the projector is aborted or the turn status is `interrupted`. Synthetic `tool.result` records are still written for transcript integrity.

**Layer 2 (output preference):** In `buildResult()`, prefer `completedTurn.error.message` over `synthesizedMissingToolResultError` so real failure reasons always surface as the headline.

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Abort + pending tool | `promptError`: missing_tool_result | `promptError`: null, `aborted: true` |
| Interrupt + pending tool | `promptError`: missing_tool_result | `promptError`: null, partial text preserved |
| Failed turn + pending tool | `promptError`: missing_tool_result | `promptError`: real turn error message |

## Testing / Proof

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
```

**149 passed** — 3 new regression tests:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| "does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError when aborted mid-exec" | Aborted + orphan commandExecution → null promptError, synthetic tool.result in trajectory |
| "does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError for interrupted turns with pending tools" | Interrupted + partial assistant text → null promptError, text preserved |
| "prefers real turn error over synthesized missing-tool-result when both are present" | Failed turn with real error + orphan tool → real error is promptError |

target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal-control sanitization across the codebase guards untrusted text before it reaches a terminal or log, preventing ANSI escape / log-forging injection (CWE-117). The canonical range is C0 (0x00–0x1f), DEL (0x7f), **and C1 (0x80–0x9f)** — the range already used by the shared `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` and by `renderTerminalBufferText` (merged in #103274). The C1 range includes the 8-bit CSI introducer **U+009B** (equivalent to `ESC [`).

Several output sinks had drifted: they covered C0/DEL but not C1, so a C1 byte (e.g. U+009B) passed through into terminal/log output. Rather than land these as isolated one-sink patches (per maintainer feedback on #103226), this is a single **deliberate, sink-wide pass**: it audits every control-character sink, closes the C1 gap in the terminal/log output sinks, and documents why the remaining sinks are already covered, out of scope, or deferred.

## Sink-wide audit

### ① Fixed here — C1 added to terminal/log output sinks (each with a focused regression test)

| Sink (function) | File | Action on control chars |
|---|---|---|
| `hasControlCharacter` (gates `buildProviderReauthCommand`) | `src/agents/failover-error.ts` | reject (suppress command) |
| `sanitizeModelWarningValue` | `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` | truncate at first control |
| `hasUnsafeControlChars` | `src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts` | gate (agent-only fallback) |
| `escapeControlCharsVisible` | `src/agents/tool-policy-audit.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `validateAttachmentName` + `describeRejectedName` | `src/agents/subagent-attachments.ts` | reject + escape diagnostic |
| `sanitizeInlineDirectiveText` | `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` | escape → `\uNNNN` |
| `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` | `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` | strip |
| `sanitizeLookupPathForLog` | `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` | replace → `?` |
| `sanitizeForConsole` | `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` | strip |
| `escapeControlCharsForTerminal` | `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `replaceLogControlCharacters` (via `formatHookErrorForLog`) | `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts` | replace → space |
| `formatDiagnosticValue` | `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` | replace → space |

Each keeps its own action; only the control-code classification is aligned with `sanitizeForLog`'s range. **Why not just call `sanitizeForLog`?** It strips *all* control + ANSI *and* removes tabs/newlines, and lacks these sinks' semantics — visible escaping, `?` replacement, boundary truncation, rejection, whitespace-flattening, length caps, and optional-value handling. The right boundary is the local predicate at each sink; this PR only completes the shared range there.

### ② Already C1-complete (unchanged, referenced for coverage)

- `sanitizeForLog` — `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` (canonical range).
- `renderTerminalBufferText` — `src/gateway/terminal/buffer-text.ts` (#103274, merged).

### ③ In-scope but deferred

- `sanitizeHookConsoleValue` — `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`. A console-warning sink that is genuinely in scope, but its only caller is inside the full gateway hook request handler; it warrants dedicated integration coverage. Deferred to a follow-up rather than shipping an untested one-liner here.

### ④ Considered and excluded (different threat model — not terminal/log output injection)

- `hasPromptUnsafeControlCharacter` — `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`: no-op for C1; the immediately-following ASCII allowlist already rejects it (this was #103401, closed).
- `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` — `src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts`: chat-message **input** sanitization routed to channels; tab/LF/CR intentionally preserved.
- `sanitizeMediaDirectiveValue` — `src/agents/internal-events.ts`: builds prompt/runtime-context text, not terminal output.
- `sanitizeArgs` — `src/plugins/commands.ts`; `stripControlChars` — `src/cli/windows-argv.ts`: argv/plugin-arg normalization (input side).
- Input/URL/JSON-validity validators (`validateNoControlChars` in acp, `hasControlOrWhitespace` in scp-host, `normalizeProviderFinalUrl` in web-fetch, `isControlCharacter` in `packages/ai` JSON escaping) — reject/validate for other reasons; C1 is not an ANSI-injection concern there.

## Testing / Proof

All twelve fixed sinks have a focused regression using a **valid** U+009B sequence (CSI + `31m`, since U+009B is itself the complete introducer — no extra `[`). Per-file `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file>` results:

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `agents/failover-error.test.ts` | 98 passed (incl. C1 provider-id rejection) |
| `agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` | 2 passed (C1 boundary truncation) |
| `agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts` | 6 passed (session-label escaping + agent-only fallback) |
| `agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts` | 3 passed (C1 name rejected + escaped diagnostic) |
| `agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` | 57 passed |
| `agents/console-sanitize.test.ts` | 3 passed |
| `commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` | 33 passed (+1 skipped) |
| `flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts` | 6 passed (`formatHookErrorForLog`) |
| `infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts` | new C1 test passes ✅ (see note) |

> Note on `config.test.ts`: four sibling `config.openFile` tests hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` (unrelated to this change) and pass on Linux CI. The new `replaces C1 control characters in the logged failed config path` test deliberately asserts only the sanitized `cfg?.json` fragment, so it is green on both platforms.

Real code-point evidence (before → after) for `sanitizeModelWarningValue`, toggling only the one-line predicate: on current `main` a providerless model `gpt4<U+0080>EVIL` logs `Model "gpt4EVIL" ...` (residual C1 dropped, attacker suffix retained); with this change it logs `Model "gpt4" ...` (truncated at the C1 boundary).

## Relationship to the open C1 PRs

This supersedes the seven isolated sink PRs (#103379 #103380 #103381 #103382 #103383 #103402 #103405) and re-lands the `sanitizeForConsole` fix from the closed #103226 cleanly (valid U+009B test, no proof-only scripts). Those PRs will be closed in favor of this consolidated review.

target.title: fix(codex): do not promote missing_tool_result on abort/interrupt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server turns that end mid-exec (user abort, steer/interrupt, or other interrupt terminals) while a native `commandExecution` is still open would fail the whole attempt with a synthesized `missing_tool_result` prompt error. Operators then saw a generic tool-invariant failure instead of abort/interrupt classification, and any partial assistant text could be treated as a failed run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fail-closed synthetic `tool.result` rows for transcript/trajectory integrity, but stop promoting that invariant to the attempt `promptError` when the authoritative outcome is already `aborted` or turn status `interrupted`. Ordinary completed turns that still lack a matching tool result continue to record `promptError` as before. Failed-turn real errors remain preferred via the existing `this.promptError` assignment on `turn.status === "failed"`.

## User Impact

When a Codex-backed turn is cancelled or interrupted while a long-running native tool is still open, the attempt keeps abort/interrupt semantics instead of dying as a generic missing-tool invariant error. Partial assistant text on interrupted turns is preserved as non-error assistant output. Transcripts still show a synthetic failed tool result for the unfinished call.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS

### Current-main refresh

Merged latest `origin/main` into this branch (no force-push) so the projector guard and tests sit on current main after recent projector-adjacent refactors.

### Focused unit / projector regression (post-merge)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts -t "does not promote missing_tool_result|records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace"
# → 3 passed (abort mid-exec, interrupted pending tool, completed orphan control)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
# → 148 passed
```

Focused proof excerpt:

```text
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError when aborted mid-exec
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError for interrupted turns with pending tools
✓ records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace assistant text and an orphan tool call
```

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(codex): keep mirrored tool results out of inline transcript updates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An internal Codex app-server tool result can be mirrored into an OpenClaw session transcript as a `toolResult` message. That durable record is useful for context, debugging, and replay, but the mirror path also published the same `toolResult` as an inline transcript-update `message`.

Live-update and source-chat delivery consumers treat inline transcript-update messages as displayable. A failed command result could therefore appear as a standalone source-chat message after an otherwise successful assistant response.

## Implementation

This change keeps `toolResult` records in the durable transcript while publishing them as sequence-only live updates:

- `user` and `assistant` records retain `update.message`;
- `toolResult` records retain `messageId` and `messageSeq`, but omit `update.message`;
- consumers can still observe transcript advancement and refresh durable state without receiving raw tool output as displayable content.

Focused regressions verify that a failed Bash result is persisted but not emitted inline, and that mixed user/tool-result/assistant batches preserve stable sequence numbers.

## Fresh Reimplementation

This refresh was not a mechanical rebase of the old implementation. The publication boundary and regressions were reimplemented from scratch on:

- current `main` at `ef13c2fe98fcca56da0948eabf1ac19128501a71`;
- installed `v2026.7.1-beta.5` at `b6387af` for runtime validation.

## Evidence

### Current main

- focused transcript-mirror suite: 26/26 passed;
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed;
- formatting, Oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed;
- full `pnpm build`: passed;
- stale-head CI failures retested on current main: 7/7 and 139/139 passed.

### Installed beta.5

- focused transcript-mirror suite: 20/20 passed;
- beta.5 full build: passed;
- patched bundle loaded by the live gateway, which continued to report `OpenClaw 2026.7.1-beta.5 (b6387af)`.

### Live Matrix regression

The original user-visible failure was recreated against the live beta.5 gateway. The browser setting was first staged absent, then successfully restored to `browser.headless: true`. This exact verification command was invoked without accepting the expected `diff` exit code 1:

```sh
jq -e '.browser.headless == true' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/openclaw.json && diff -u <(jq '.browser' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/backups/pr99042-live-validation-20260712-062129/openclaw.json.headless-absent-test) <(jq '.browser' /Users/[REDACTED]/.openclaw/openclaw.json)
```

The trajectory recorded `status: failed`, `isError: true`, and exit code 1 while the intended headless configuration remained active. Matrix readback showed no standalone `Bash failed` or tool-result message.

Post-turn Matrix audit: **PASSED** at `2026-07-12T03:58Z`. The expected final reply was Matrix event `$oHhexSCRmWR1jlT4tKzUq8xYll1qqTrb0KQYYoKYRe8`; no standalone [REDACTED] message containing `Bash failed`, `toolResult`, or `tool result` appeared after the failed tool event. The trajectory still records `status: failed`, `isError: true`, and exit code 1, while `browser.headless` remains `true`.

## Risk

Low-to-medium. The change affects only the live publication shape of Codex app-server mirrored tool-result records. Durable transcript persistence, message sequencing, user/assistant publication, dedupe behavior, and explicit message-tool delivery remain unchanged.

## Non-Goals

- Do not remove tool results from session transcripts.
- Do not suppress user or assistant mirror updates.
- Do not change explicit delivery initiated through messaging tools.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard direct wiki reads and share supplement registry
target.body:
Related: #101809
Supersedes: #101943

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_get` with `corpus=wiki` would crash the tool run as an unhandled rejection when a registered wiki corpus supplement's `get()` threw (for example config or backend failure), instead of returning a structured disabled error.

Also resolves a problem where Gateway-loaded plugins could register corpus supplements in one module instance while `memory-core` tools read from another empty registry after module reload, so `corpus=wiki` / `corpus=all` lookups could silently miss registered wiki supplements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Guard the direct `corpus=wiki` read path with try-catch and surface the backend failure via `formatErrorMessage()`, matching the structured `{ disabled: true, error }` contract already used for missing wiki results. Store memory plugin state via `resolveGlobalSingleton(Symbol.for("openclaw.memoryPluginState"))` so Gateway and plugin loaders share one registry across reloads.

Out of scope: supplement search fail-fast (`#77897`, open PR #78035) and the already-merged `corpus=all` fallback guard (#101902).

## User Impact

Agents and operators calling `memory_get corpus=wiki` get a clear disabled error when the wiki backend fails, instead of an unhandled rejection. Wiki/memory corpus supplements remain visible after Gateway plugin reloads.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `14e685d1` (`14e685d181e9936df7d6c1d640d7967005389e05`)

Rank-up: replaced hand-rolled `globalThis` resolver with `resolveGlobalSingleton` and added duplicate-module clear/restore coverage for capability + corpus + prompt state.

**Unit tests (focused):**

```
✓ returns structured error when corpus=wiki supplement get throws
✓ shares corpus supplement registry through globalThis across module reloads
✓ shares clear and restore across duplicate module instances
```

Commands:

```

pnpm test src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts -t "globalThis across module reloads"
```

target.title: Fix stack-safe large attachment handling
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #90098.

This branch is now rebased onto current OpenClaw architecture and deliberately narrowed to the parts still missing from `main`:

- replace the gateway's full-payload data-URL capture regex with bounded index/slice parsing;
- replace the Control UI send-path data-URL capture regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`;
- replace the pasted-image full-payload regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts` with a bounded header check plus iterative payload validation;
- discard stale failed composer queue entries created by the old `Maximum call stack size exceeded` failure;
- add focused gateway and current-UI regression coverage.

Current `main` already contains iterative base64 validation and the broader 20 MB / 20-page inbound extraction policy, so this update keeps those upstream implementations and drops the obsolete extraction-limit/config churn from the older branch.

## What problem this solves

Multi-megabyte PDF/image data URLs were still passed through regexes that captured the entire base64 payload. On sufficiently large browser or gateway sends, V8 could throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the attachment reached normal validation/offload handling. Failed Control UI sends carrying that historical error could also be restored and replayed after upgrade.

The new parsing keeps regex use bounded to a short MIME header and processes the payload by index/iteration.

## Current changed paths

- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`
- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`

## Evidence

Exact head after conflict repair: `f797fa0846a3081671a4e714dbf622c3a2a1dc90`.

Conflict-resolution proof:

- Merged current `origin/main` into the PR branch and resolved the only conflict in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`.
- Kept the stack-safe bounded `stripBase64DataUrlPrefix` index/slice path; did not reintroduce the full-payload data-URL capture regex.
- Verified no unmerged paths and no conflict markers in the touched Gateway/UI areas before commit.

Exact-head behavior/regression proof:

- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` -> 4 test files, 124 tests passed. This includes the 12 MiB Gateway data URL parse/offload regression and the bounded parser path.
- `pnpm --dir ui test -- src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-state.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` -> 226 test files, 3,561 tests passed. This covers large Control UI attachment serialization, pasted-image conversion/rejection, queue restore, marker preservation, and public snapshot stripping in the current UI layout.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts` -> clean.
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed after adding the valid `schema_version` numeric SQLite pragma to the test helper, clearing the latest-base CI failure.

Upgrade-cleanup proof on exact head:

- The focused composer-persistence/chat-state/send tests demonstrate that an unmarked legacy failed attachment record carrying the historical stack-overflow signature is removed during restore.
- The same focused tests demonstrate that a newly marked failed attachment record remains durable/retryable, and that the storage-only marker is stripped from public queue snapshots.

Real-behavior caveat:

- The earlier real Chrome/Gateway upload proof remains a pre-port live run. This exact-head update adds current-head runtime regression proof over the Gateway, Control UI send, composer paste, and queue-migration paths, but I am not making a new live provider/device claim for this merge-conflict repair.

## Verification

Regression coverage on the current file layout now includes:

- a 12 MiB gateway data URL parsed/offloaded without a full-payload regex;
- a large Control UI attachment serialized through `chat.send`;
- a large pasted image converted through the current composer;
- rejection of invalid pasted base64;
- identifiable pre-fix attachment stack-overflow records dropped during restore, while current failures and unrelated text failures with the same generic V8 phrase remain durable and retryable via a stored item-format marker.

Fresh GitHub CI is running on exact head `f797fa0846a3081671a4e714dbf622c3a2a1dc90`, which merges current `origin/main` and preserves the narrowed legacy-cleanup repair.

Additional exact-head repair validation: 124 focused Gateway tests pass; 3,562 focused Control UI chat tests pass across composer persistence, chat state, chat send, and chat view; targeted formatting and `pnpm check:test-types` also pass; hosted `check-lint` is running on this final head. The storage-only marker is retained across internal normalization only for affected failed attachment records and is stripped from public queue snapshots.

## Real behavior evidence

The original branch was validated with a real Chrome upload of a 9.18 MB, 8-page PDF (roughly a 12 MB base64 data URL) against a live gateway. The upload completed without `RangeError`, was offloaded, and the model received extracted page content. That live run was on the pre-port head; this update ports the same stack-safe parsing behavior to today's gateway and UI paths and adds exact-path regression tests. No new live Signal/provider/device claim is being made for this merge-only port.

Generated with AI assistance; all security-sensitive parsing remains fail-closed for malformed payloads.

target.title: fix(hooks): report agent startup admission failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/hooks/agent` could return HTTP success as soon as an isolated agent run was queued, even if the run failed before reaching runner-entry/session admission. For Symphony Kanban this made a hook dispatch look durable while the worker had actually hit a lifecycle/startup failure such as:

`Session "agent:herbert-karajan:hook:symphony-kanban" changed while starting work. Retry.`

That left the board with an accepted dispatch but no reliable worker closeout path.

This PR changes agent hook dispatch so startup/admission failures surface through the HTTP response before the idempotency key is cached:

- waits for `onExecutionStarted` before returning `{ ok: true, runId }`
- returns `409` for changed/deleted/archived session startup failures
- returns `503` if runner entry does not start before the admission timeout
- returns `502` for other pre-start failures
- keeps post-start failures on the existing async/log/system-event path
- preserves hook session-key policy and `deliver:false` behavior

## Evidence

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/gateway/hooks.test.ts src/gateway/hooks-mapping.test.ts src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts src/gateway/server/hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`
  - passed: 16 files / 314 tests
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
  - passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
  - passed

## Operational Boundary

This is source-only. It does not restart or modify any live gateway config by itself. Runtime activation still requires the normal deployment path and an approved gateway refresh.

## Related Tracking

- KAN-278: implementation card for the hook-session routing/admission fix.
- KAN-223: live worker smoke target after merge/deploy/gateway refresh.
- KAN-267: superseded duplicate investigation card.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.


Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
```


## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
